rawFindings.title: Incorrect URL_REGEXP breaks relative URL matching in error formatter
rawFindings.explanation: The original regex matched URLs optionally starting with domain and allowed paths starting with optional slash. The changed regex matches URLs starting necessarily with 'http://' and a domain, requiring '/' after domain, thus failing to match relative URLs without domain.
rawFindings.suggestion: Restore the original regex that optionally matches URLs starting with 'http://' and domain, and also matches relative URLs starting with optional slash, to correctly identify URLs in error messages.

rawFindings.title: Incorrect URL_REGEXP pattern causes failed relative URL matching
rawFindings.explanation: The original regex matched optional http and optional domain for URLs, allowing matching of relative URLs like '/base/path'. The changed regex requires 'http://' and domain, so URLs without 'http://' (like '/base/b.js') no longer match, breaking relative URL handling.
rawFindings.suggestion: Restore original regex pattern to allow matching URLs with optional http domain, e.g., revert line 24 to: var URL_REGEXP = new RegExp('(?:http:\/\/[^\/]*)?\/?' + ... );

acceptedFindings.title: Incorrect URL_REGEXP pattern causes failed relative URL matching
acceptedFindings.explanation: The original regex matched optional http and optional domain for URLs, allowing matching of relative URLs like '/base/path'. The changed regex requires 'http://' and domain, so URLs without 'http://' (like '/base/b.js') no longer match, breaking relative URL handling.
acceptedFindings.suggestion: Restore original regex pattern to allow matching URLs with optional http domain, e.g., revert line 24 to: var URL_REGEXP = new RegExp('(?:http:\/\/[^\/]*)?\/?' + ... );

rawFindings.title: Incorrect URL_REGEXP alteration breaks matching relative URLs
rawFindings.explanation: The original regular expression "(?:http:\/\/[^\/]*)?\/?" allowed matching both URLs with and without the protocol and domain, including relative paths starting with '/base' or '/absolute'. The changed RegExp "http:\/\/[^\/]*\/" requires the URL to start explicitly with 'http://' and a domain, failing to match relative URLs like '/base/b.js'. This can break error message formatting where relative URLs are common.
rawFindings.suggestion: Restore the original RegExp or adjust it to allow matching both absolute (with http://) and relative URLs (starting with '/') as before.
